heading: Strict role folders and file names
body: A role type has a domain prefix and a standard suffix. Its file name matches the type name exactly, including case. Its direct parent folder has the plural role name. Examples are MoneyService in services/MoneyService.ts, MoneyStore in stores/MoneyStore.ts and MoneySetup in setups/MoneySetup.ts. Each annotated file holds exactly one class and its imports. Helper types and functions belong in their own files. Each realm has shared role folders, and the two realms use the same folder names. Yon uses server/services, server/stores, server/clients, server/setups, server/entities, server/helpers and server/converters. Tac uses the same seven under client/. Controllers live in server/controllers, one class in each file. A role file in the wrong folder fails with TY1310. The error names the shared folder where the file belongs. The compiler validates the selected files from the snapshot of the source, which cannot change, and puts them together. Role annotations register validated declarations inside that entry scope. Modifiers such as CacheSettings, Setting, Table and Settings add no naming rules. Native Tac keeps its service type first and uses only public client modules. See the Strict annotation layout guide for every supported language.
